lesson_title: From Doodle to Blueprint in One Lesson
hook_text: A rough sketch of a rescue claw. By the end of the lesson, anyone could build it from the drawings. Here is how.
clip_script: Start with the sketch: base, two arms crossing at a pivot, a syringe pushing a rod, jaws at the front. Now make it real. Measure the syringe first, because you cannot change it: 110 long, plunger moves 70. So the base is 300 by 120, double card. Arms 200 by 25, doubled so they do not bend. Pivot 60 from the tip for grip, or 80 for a wider opening; choose and write why. Then draw it twice. Oblique: side view as the front face, feint lines, 45 degree depth on the grid, dark outlines, labels from plunger to jaw. Working drawing: one view, scale 1 to 2, every real size in millimetres, holes located, a parts list beside it. Two drawings, and a classmate could build your device without you in the room. That is what design marks are made of.
visual_style: Whiteboard sketch morphing into an oblique drawing with labels, then a flat dimensioned top view with a parts list filling in alongside.
mood: Purposeful and encouraging, the project becoming concrete.
pacing: Sizes fixed in quick beats, oblique drawing built step by step, working drawing and list to finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and finish both drawings of your rescue device this week.
